result.title: Beyond Scarcity: When Encoder Adaptation Is Worthwhile
result.summary: Long-tailed recognition often learns a shared representation before correcting the classifier for class imbalance. Once the classifier has been rebalanced, however, final accuracy does not reveal whether further encoder adaptation remains worthwhile. Standard imbalance benchmarks obscure this question because they jointly vary the number of distinct examples available to rare classes and the frequency with which those examples shape the representation. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework that separates unique support from representation allocation and estimates the incremental value of encoder updates through matched classifier-only and full-network continuations from a common corrected model. The framework combines stage-specific controls, multiple representation and adaptation objectives, whole-distribution metrics, and hierarchical inference over class assignments, support reconstructions, and optimization runs. Across the controlled study, the same low-support regime moves from one in which classifier-only training is adequate to one in which encoder adaptation yields a practically meaningful benefit solely as representation allocation becomes more imbalanced. The transition persists across classifier corrections, representation objectives, normalization and augmentation controls, and ImageNet-scale evaluation, while preserving frequent-class accuracy. Under the prespecified one-percentage-point operating margin, the two regimes are separated by simultaneous confidence bounds. These results show that benchmark construction can alter a post-correction training decision and that support size alone does not characterize the remaining value of representation adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究长尾识别中分类器重平衡后编码器是否仍值得继续适配，提出受控评测框架，将「独特样本支撑量」与「表征分配」解耦，并用匹配的分类器-only 与全网络续训来估计编码器更新的增量价值。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「匹配续训 + 受控变量」的增量价值估计思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中收益究竟来自 latent 状态更新还是答案读出端，但从纯视觉分类任务迁移到多模态推理仍需较多改造验证。
